description:
CAN bus network schematic sheet titled "CAN D STBD" (drawing 196D5023, sheet 31 of 47, BAE Systems, Endicott NY). This is a daisy-chain CAN bus backbone diagram showing a series of "CAN Y CONNECTOR" tee/tap points wired in series along a thick black backbone line, with each Y-connector dropping down (or branching) to a device/node connected to that segment of the CAN bus. The bus is terminated at both ends with 120-Ohm CAN terminator resistors.

Topology (left to right, following the backbone from the terminated end at column H down to the branch/isolator section):
1. CAN Terminator 120 Ohm (leftmost/end-of-bus termination) connects to a CAN Y CONNECTOR, which branches to "24V RTN to CAN shield" — a note calls out that CAN Shield Ground should be located as close as possible to the 24V ground terminal without extending the CAN backbone (red warning note).
2. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to CAN Y CONNECTOR → ALARM NAV (a secondary tap/stub off the main connector).
3. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to SCU.
4. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to DISPLAY NAV.
5. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to ESS.
6. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to EDM STBD.
7. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to HCP.
8. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to ECP3.
9. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to ECP4.
10. Next CAN Y CONNECTOR branches to BCP.

The backbone then turns (routed via a right-angle jog) down to a CAN Y CONNECTOR (mid-sheet, column F/E) which branches down through an ISOLATOR to another CAN Y CONNECTOR, which branches to BEL4 and also continues to a CAN Terminator 120 Ohm (terminating this branch of the bus).

In parallel, a second CAN Y CONNECTOR (column D) branches down through a second ISOLATOR to another CAN Y CONNECTOR, which branches to BEL3 and also continues to a CAN Terminator 120 Ohm (terminating this branch).

The two isolator branches' upper CAN Y CONNECTORS are also tied together and continue up/right to another CAN Y CONNECTOR (column C) which branches to MC43, and continues to CIB STBD, which connects to "ENG STBD with 120 Ohm" (engine module with internal/associated 120 Ohm termination).

This is a CAN bus (Controller Area Network) topology diagram, not a power distribution schematic - there are no breakers/fuses shown; the "CAN Y CONNECTOR" blocks represent physical tee connectors/splices on the data bus, and "ISOLATOR" blocks are CAN bus isolators (galvanic isolation devices) inserted in-line on certain branches. Terminators (120 Ohm resistors) are placed at the physical ends of the bus segments per standard CAN bus termination practice.

Devices tapped onto this CAN D STBD bus: BCP, ECP4, ECP3, HCP, EDM STBD, ESS, DISPLAY NAV, SCU, ALARM NAV, BEL4, BEL3, MC43, CIB STBD, ENG STBD (with 120 Ohm), plus a 24V RTN to CAN shield ground reference point.

Title block: Drawing No. 196D5023, Size D, Sheet 31 of 47, Contract No. Not Applicable, Warning: Export Controlled - See Title Page, CAGE Code 89954, BAE Systems Endicott NY, Controls/G.Zaleski, Scale: None, See Sheet 1 for related info. No revisions listed (Rev -). No cross-reference to other specific drawing numbers is legible except "SEE SHEET 1" and "SEE TITLE PAGE" notes in title block.

Red engineering note (upper left area): "NOTE: CAN Shield Ground should be located as close as possible to the 24V ground terminal without extending the CAN backbone."
